The arc length of a curve $y=f(x)$ between $x=a$ and $x=b$ can be found using the formula

$$
L={\int }_{a}^{b}\sqrt{1+[{f}^{′}(x)]^{2}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $f(x)=\frac{{x}^{2}}{8}-\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x),$ $a=1,$ and $b=2.$

First, we find the derivative of $f(x):$

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=\frac{x}{4}-\frac{1}{x}
$$

Now, let's compute $\sqrt{1+[{f}^{′}(x)]^{2}}:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{1+[{f}^{′}(x)]^{2}} & =\sqrt{1+{(\frac{x}{4}-\frac{1}{x})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+(\frac{{x}^{2}}{16}-\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{{x}^{2}}{16}+\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{{x}^{4}+8{x}^{2}+16}{16{x}^{2}}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{({x}^{2}+4)^{2}}{16{x}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}+4}{4x}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $\sqrt{1+[{f}^{′}(x)]^{2}}=\frac{{x}^{2}+4}{4x}$ into the arc length formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\sqrt{1+[{f}^{′}(x)]^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{{x}^{2}+4}{4x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}(\frac{x}{4}+\frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(\frac{{x}^{2}}{8}+\operatorname{ln}⁡x)|}_{1}^{2} \\  & =[\frac{{2}^{2}}{8}+\operatorname{ln}⁡2]-[\frac{{1}^{2}}{8}+\operatorname{ln}⁡1] \\  & =\frac{3}{8}+\operatorname{ln}⁡2.\end{aligned}
$$

The arc length of a curve y=f(x) between x=a and x=b can be found using the formula L=∫ab1+[f′(x)]2dx.

In our case, f(x)=x28−ln⁡(2x), a=1, and b=2.

First, we find the derivative of f(x): f′(x)=x4−1x

Now, let's compute 1+[f′(x)]2: 1+[f′(x)]2=1+(x4−1x)2=1+(x216−12+1x2)=x216+12+1x2=x4+8x2+1616x2=(x2+4)216x2=x2+44x Substituting 1+[f′(x)]2=x2+44x into the arc length formula, we get L=∫121+[f′(x)]2dx=∫12x2+44xdx=∫12(x4+1x)dx=(x28+ln⁡x)|12=[228+ln⁡2]−[128+ln⁡1]=38+ln⁡2.
